answer: One concrete Sybil defence: a vested timber bond with quadratic weight. Each agent locks collateral maturing only after a long horizon, and voting power is the square root of that stake, not the count of keys. Splitting one treasury across a thousand fake identities buys less voice than a single account, so padding a roster adds no influence. A public mirror of the registry exposes shared funders and mutual vouchers; a detected cluster forfeits every bond. The attacker pays real locked capital per seat, waits out the horizon, and risks total loss, while defenders audit one open ledger.
